info.title: About this app
info.subtitle: Version, update channel and updates
info.channel_production_hint: Stable releases from the main branch.
info.channel_test_hint: Builds from the test branch: newest features, possibly rough edges.
info.downgrade_warning: This version is older than the installed one. Going back only works when the database schema is compatible; a database backup is made first.
info.updater_unavailable: Updating from the interface works on an installed server (Debian 13 with the installer).
info.install_confirm: The app downloads {{tag}}, backs up the database, migrates it and restarts. That takes about a minute. If the new version doesn't start, it rolls back automatically.
info.state_failed: Update failed and was rolled back

users.title: Users
users.subtitle: Who can sign in, and what they may do.
users.role_admin_hint: Can change everything, including users, backups and updates.
users.role_viewer_hint: Can look at everything, but not change settings.
users.active_hint: Disabled users can't sign in and their sessions end.

backups.title: Backups
backups.subtitle: Full and incremental backups of the app to FTP, FTPS, SFTP or SCP, with restore from the remote location.
backups.empty_text: Add a location such as your NAS or a storage box. The app then makes a full backup weekly and incremental ones in between.
backups.delete_confirm: Remove backup location {{name}}? Backups already on it stay there.
backups.name: Name
backups.ftp_warning: Plain FTP sends your password unencrypted. Use FTPS or SFTP where you can, and turn on backup encryption.
backups.ftps_implicit_hint: Usually port 990. Off means explicit TLS (AUTH TLS) on port 21.
backups.verify_tls_hint: Turn off only for self-signed certificates on your own network.
backups.encryption_hint: Backups are encrypted with AES-256-GCM before they leave the server. Keep this passphrase safe: without it a backup can't be restored.
backups.cron_hint: Times in UTC. Empty = not scheduled.
backups.keep_full_hint: Older chains are removed after a new full backup.
backups.restore_subtitle: These backups are on the remote location. Incremental backups are restored together with their full backup.
backups.remote_empty: No backups found on this location.
backups.restore_warning: Users, settings and history go back to {{date}}. A safety copy of the current database is made first and put back if the restore fails.

mail.title: Mail server
mail.subtitle: The SMTP server this app uses for password resets and notifications.
mail.security_starttls_hint: Recommended: connects on 587 and upgrades to TLS. The connection is refused if the server doesn't offer TLS.
mail.security_tls_hint: SMTPS: TLS from the first byte, usually port 465.
mail.security_none_hint: Only for a relay on your own network.
mail.username_hint: Leave empty for a relay without authentication.
mail.verify_tls_hint: Checks the server certificate and host name.
mail.no_tls_warning: Without TLS, passwords and emails travel unencrypted.
mail.dkim_hint: Sign outgoing mail so receivers can verify it really comes from your domain.
mail.dkim_key_hint: RSA or Ed25519 key in PEM format. Publish the public key at <selector>._domainkey.<domain>.
mail.test_hint: Uses the values in the form, also before you save them.
mail.test_failed: The test email could not be sent

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.subtitle: Who gets an email when something happens.
notifications.backup_failure_to_hint: Recommended. Leave empty for no email.
notifications.update_to_hint: Sent once after a new version starts.

general.title: General
general.subtitle: Name and address of the app.
general.base_url_hint: The address people (and AI apps) use, for example https://mcp.example.com. Used in emails and for OAuth. Leave empty to use the address of the request.

web.title: Web server & proxy
web.subtitle: How the app is reached: directly with its own HTTPS, or behind a reverse proxy such as Zoraxy.
web.mode_proxy_hint: The proxy handles HTTPS. Nginx listens on plain HTTP and trusts X-Forwarded-For and X-Forwarded-Proto only from the addresses below.
web.mode_direct_hint: Nginx serves HTTPS itself on port 443 and redirects HTTP to HTTPS.
web.trusted_proxies_hint: IP address or range of Zoraxy, one per line, e.g. 10.10.4.2 or 10.10.4.0/24.
web.restrict: Only accept traffic from the proxy
web.restrict_hint: Blocks direct access that bypasses Zoraxy.
web.cert_hint: Default is a self-signed certificate. For Let's Encrypt run certbot on the server and enter its paths here.
web.base_path_hint: / for the root, or e.g. /mmn to serve the app at https://host/mmn.
web.dev_note: On a development machine the settings are saved, but Nginx is configured only on an installed server.
web.apply_failed: Applying failed; the previous configuration is still active
web.not_https: The app sees this request as plain HTTP. Check that the proxy address is correct and that Zoraxy sends X-Forwarded-Proto.
web.zoraxy_1: In Zoraxy, add an HTTP proxy rule for your host name, e.g. mcp.example.com.
web.zoraxy_2: Target: the IP of this server on port 80 (Zoraxy connected from {{ip}}).
web.zoraxy_3: Turn on TLS/HTTPS with a certificate for the host name (Zoraxy can request one via ACME).
web.zoraxy_4: Leave WebSocket support on and do not strip headers (X-Forwarded-For, X-Forwarded-Proto, Host).
web.zoraxy_5: Enter Zoraxy's IP address above and set the public address under General.

ai.connections_subtitle: AI apps that may work with this server through MCP.
ai.connected_apps_hint: Connected through OAuth: you approved them on the consent page.
ai.no_connections_hint: Connect Claude, ChatGPT or Copilot in a few steps.
ai.tokens_subtitle: Personal tokens for MCP clients that use a fixed token, and for scripts.
ai.no_tokens_hint: Most AI apps sign in with OAuth and don't need a token. Create one for scripts or clients without OAuth.
ai.token_name_hint: So you recognise it in the activity log.
ai.revoke_confirm: Revoke token {{name}}? Clients using it stop working.
ai.token_once: Copy this token now. It is shown only once and stored only as a hash.
ai.token_next: Next: add it to your MCP client, see

ai.activity_empty_hint: As soon as an AI app uses the MCP server, its actions appear here.

audit.title: Audit log
audit.subtitle: Everything that changed, from the interface, via AI or by the system.

help.title: Help & guides
help.subtitle: How things work, and how to connect an AI.
help.topic_mcp_text: Step by step: let an AI app work with this server through the built-in MCP server.
help.topic_backups_text: A full backup stores everything; incremental backups store only what changed since. A restore takes the full backup plus the incrementals up to the moment you pick.
help.topic_updates_text: Open Info & updates at the bottom of the menu. Production follows the main branch, Test the test branch. Updates back up the database first and roll back automatically when the new version doesn't start.
help.topic_proxy_text: Under Web server & proxy you choose between own HTTPS and running behind Zoraxy, and you see what the app receives from the proxy.
help.topic_security_text: Passwords are hashed with Argon2id, stored secrets are encrypted, sessions use secure cookies with CSRF protection, and every change is in the audit log.

mcphelp.title: Connect an AI to the MCP server
mcphelp.subtitle: Let Claude, ChatGPT or Copilot answer questions about this server and carry out tasks. You decide what each app may do.
mcphelp.local_title: Cloud AI apps need a public HTTPS address
mcphelp.local_text: Claude (web and app) and ChatGPT connect from their own cloud, so they can't reach a local or plain-HTTP address. Publish the app through Zoraxy with a domain and certificate and set the public address under General. Claude Code and VS Code run on your own computer and also work on your local network.
mcphelp.claude_desc: Add it once as a custom connector; it then works in every chat.
mcphelp.claude_2: Click Add custom connector and give it a name, e.g. MCP Management Node.
mcphelp.claude_4: Click Add and then Connect. You're sent to this app: sign in, pick the permissions and click Allow access.
mcphelp.claude_5: In a chat, turn the connector on via the tools menu and ask for example: “Which backups ran this week?”
mcphelp.claude_desktop_note: Custom connectors are available on Claude's paid plans; in Team and Enterprise an owner may need to allow them first.
mcphelp.claude_desktop_token: Claude Desktop with a local address (without OAuth)
mcphelp.claude_desktop_token_text: Create an API token, then add this to <c>claude_desktop_config.json</c> (Settings → Developer → Edit config). It needs Node.js on your computer.
mcphelp.cc_desc: Claude in your terminal. Runs on your own computer, so a local address works too.
mcphelp.cc_2: Start Claude Code, type /mcp, choose mcp-node and then Authenticate.
mcphelp.cc_3: Your browser opens this app: sign in and click Allow access. Done.
mcphelp.with_token: With an API token instead of OAuth
mcphelp.with_token_text: Create a token under API tokens and pass it as a header:
mcphelp.chatgpt_desc: Via developer mode, available in ChatGPT's paid plans.
mcphelp.chatgpt_1: Open Settings → Apps & Connectors → Advanced settings and turn on Developer mode.
mcphelp.chatgpt_2: Go back to Apps & Connectors and click Create.
mcphelp.chatgpt_3: Give it a name and enter the MCP Server URL:
mcphelp.chatgpt_4: Choose OAuth as authentication, tick that you trust the application and click Create.
mcphelp.chatgpt_5: Sign in to this app in the window that opens, pick the permissions and click Allow access. In a chat, add the connector via + → Developer mode.
mcphelp.chatgpt_note: ChatGPT asks for your confirmation before it runs a tool that changes something.
mcphelp.copilot_desc: Use the tools in Copilot's agent mode.
mcphelp.copilot_1: Create .vscode/mcp.json in your project (or run MCP: Add Server from the command palette):
mcphelp.copilot_2: Click Start above the server in mcp.json. VS Code asks you to sign in: allow it, approve in this app and click Allow access.
mcphelp.copilot_3: Open Copilot Chat, switch to Agent mode and check under the tools icon that mcp-node is on.
mcphelp.copilot_4: For Copilot Business or Enterprise, an admin must allow MCP servers in Copilot in the organisation policy.
mcphelp.copilot_token_text: Prefer a token? VS Code asks for it once and stores it securely:
mcphelp.other_desc: The server follows the MCP standard.
mcphelp.other_1: Transport: Streamable HTTP at the address above (JSON responses, stateless).
mcphelp.other_2: OAuth 2.1: discovery at /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource, dynamic client registration and PKCE.
mcphelp.other_3: Or a token: header Authorization: Bearer mmn_… from the API tokens page.
mcphelp.safety_1: Each AI app gets only the permissions you tick; read-only is the default.
mcphelp.safety_2: Destructive actions such as a restore or an update require the AI to confirm the exact target.
mcphelp.safety_3: Every call is in the AI activity log: which app, which token, parameters, result and duration.
mcphelp.safety_4: Disconnect an app or revoke a token and it loses access immediately.
mcphelp.try_1: Is there an update for MCP Management Node?
mcphelp.try_2: Did last night's backup succeed? Show the last five runs.
mcphelp.try_3: Make a full backup to the NAS now.
mcphelp.try_4: Check the mail settings and send me a test email.
